text: It is important to note that only IL-6 and IL-8 have been shown to be released from skeletal muscle in the absence of damaging exercise (35). Many other myokines may play a role in the hypertrophic response to EIMD. Systemic IL-15 levels and IL-15 mRNA in skeletal muscle are markedly elevated after eccentric (but not concentric) exercise, giving credence to the notion that elevations are contingent on damage to fibers (27, 224). Some studies show that IL-15 directly regulates hypertrophy by increasing muscle protein synthesis and reducing proteolysis in differentiated myotubes (197, 221), although these findings recently have been challenged (219).
